reviewer.agent: Claude Code (file handoff; environment names the handoff channel)

themes.label: UN as main channel for AI governance
themes.definition: The UN is endorsed as the main channel for creating AI governance frameworks, standards and norms.
themes.inclusion: Include passages naming the UN as the principal venue or channel for global AI governance.
themes.exclusion: Exclude calls for international rules that do not specify the UN.
themes.boundary_cases: A passage fragment that completes a sentence about the UN serving as the main channel counts even if split across passages.

examples.quote: the main channel to create a widely accepted artificial intelligence governance framework, standards and norms
China supports the United Nations role as the main channel for global AI governance

themes.label: International AI rules and governance initiatives
themes.definition: Calls for widely recognized international AI rules, faster governance rules, and national proposals such as a Global AI Governance Initiative or world AI cooperation organization, respecting all countries' practices.
themes.inclusion: Include calls for international AI rules/standards or proposals for new international AI governance institutions.
themes.boundary_cases: Emphasis on respecting each country's governance principles may also indicate AI_SOVEREIGNTY_CONCENTRATION concerns.

examples.quote: China has proposed the Global AI Governance Initiative and advocated the establishment of a world AI cooperation organization.
on the basis of full respect for the governance principles and practices of all countries

themes.label: People-centred AI for good
themes.definition: AI should follow a people-centred approach, be developed 'for good', and balance development and security.
themes.inclusion: Include passages invoking people-centred, human-centred or 'AI for good' principles.
themes.exclusion: Exclude passages focused solely on institutions without normative principles.
themes.boundary_cases: Principles like 'equitable benefits' also overlap with AI_DIGITAL_DIVIDE.

examples.quote: China is committed to taking a people-centred approach, developing AI for good and putting equal emphasis on development and security

themes.label: AI capacity-building for developing countries
themes.definition: Commitments to international cooperation on AI capacity-building, e.g., an AI Capacity-Building Action Plan.
themes.inclusion: Include offers or plans for AI capacity-building cooperation.
themes.exclusion: Exclude general development cooperation not tied to AI.
themes.boundary_cases: Training programs in non-AI fields (culture) are excluded.

examples.quote: China has put forth the AI Capacity-Building Action Plan for Good and for All

themes.label: Narrowing digital divide for universal benefit
themes.definition: AI development should narrow the digital divide and deliver universally beneficial development.
themes.inclusion: Include calls to narrow the digital divide or ensure equitable AI benefits.
themes.exclusion: Exclude development agenda passages with no AI or digital reference.
themes.boundary_cases: Global South support framed without AI belongs elsewhere.

examples.quote: narrow the digital divide, and promote development that is universally beneficial

themes.label: Emerging tech brings benefits and risks
themes.definition: AI and other emerging technologies framed as bringing benefits along with potential risks.
themes.inclusion: Include explicit benefit-and-risk framings of AI.
themes.boundary_cases: If AI appears alongside biomanufacturing and network communications, still code here when duality is explicit.

examples.quote: Along with the benefits, they also bring potential risks.

value.rationale: China's passages consistently support the UN as the main channel for AI governance, people-centred 'AI for good', capacity-building and narrowing the digital divide, plus its own governance initiatives; one 2023 passage is arms-control context leading into the AI sentence.
